item.title: Iran Philippines FMs discuss bilateral ties regional developments
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Maria Theresa P. Lazaro, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of the Philippines, on Saturday evening. During the meeting, the Iranian foreign minister outlined the latest developments in the region and Iran’s efforts to restore peace and security. Lazaro expressed hope that insecurity would come to an end as soon as possible and that peace and lasting stability would return to the region. The foreign ministers of Iran and the Philippines also exchanged views on expanding Tehran-Manila bilateral relations in various areas of mutual interest.

item.title: UN humanitarian affairs chief meets Iranian Foreign Minister in New York
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs, on Saturday evening. During the meeting, regional and international developments, the humanitarian assistance situation in crisis-hit areas, and areas of cooperation between Iran and relevant UN bodies were reviewed. The Iranian foreign minister, referring to Iran’s long-standing hosting of Afghan refugees despite the US economic war and unjust sanctions, highlighted the responsibility of international humanitarian organizations in this regard. Araghchi also referred to the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the West Bank resulting from the genocide and crimes committed by the Israeli regime, as well as the displacement of hundreds of thousands of people in Lebanon due to Israel’s ongoing attacks, stressing the need for greater attention by the United Nations and international humanitarian organizations to these situations. Araghchi recalled that addressing humanitarian crises and disasters in a fundamental manner requires tackling the causes and factors that give rise to them. The UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs, for his part, outlined the most important humanitarian situations around the world and stressed the continuation of UN efforts to fulfill its humanitarian responsibilities.

🔹 Our participation in this year’s General Assembly was very active. The President left and returned this morning, but his presence was very active, with numerous meetings, numerous interviews, and that very strong speech he delivered at the Assembly. 🔹 Alongside him, I also held numerous meetings, which you have certainly followed in the news. In all these meetings, our main focus was to state the conditions of the Islamic Republic of Iran for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and for the advancement of the negotiations—conditions that have been set by the Supreme National Security Council. 🔹 We were tasked with explaining and presenting these conditions here and defending them. Thankfully, this was formally done in all the meetings we held. In the meetings we had with the mediators, these conditions were fully conveyed, explained and elaborated upon, and they also conveyed these matters to the American side. 🔹 We defended our positions, our policy and the conditions we had set in all the meetings, and the entire world, particularly fair-minded countries around the world, became aware that the Islamic Republic of Iran, just as it has defended its country well, has consistently demonstrated strength in the diplomatic arena as well, and in particular, by presenting various proposals and establishing a diplomatic path, has been able to steer the diplomatic environment in its own favor. 🔹 The proposals we put forward were discussed in interviews, explained and also raised in the meetings. They were also conveyed to the American side through intermediaries. 🔹 We saw the first reaction from the US president, but nothing has yet been conveyed to us by the mediators. Of course, the US president has also made many positive statements as well as many contradictory ones, which, unfortunately, we hear from him quite often. We are waiting for the definitive views to be conveyed to us through the intermediaries, and we will make a decision based on them. 🔹 In any case, our conditions are clear, and any move forward toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon these conditions being met, and we will not back down from them. 🔹 The outlook for the Iranian people is a bright one. The Iranian people have demonstrated their strength in the military arena, the diplomatic arena, and also in the economic arena and in confronting sanctions. 🔹 Our enemies have also tried every possible path; they pursued every avenue they could and failed to achieve results. There will be no way forward other than a negotiated solution based on dignity and justice, while securing the rights of the Iranian people and meeting their legitimate demands. 🔹 Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this impasse. This is our position. Many countries share this position with us and understand it. 🔹 There is no one in the world today who can accuse the Islamic Republic of Iran of not having tried the path of diplomacy. In this respect, we are in a stronger political position, because we have never closed the path of diplomacy or negotiations, while at the same time we have never backed down from our rights. 🔹 Whenever our enemies chose another path, we also stood firmly against them on that path.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Mr. Khalil-ur-Rehman, President of the UN General Assembly, at noon on Saturday. During the meeting, the Foreign Minister congratulated Mr. Khalil-ur-Rehman on his election as President of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly and stressed the importance of the General Assembly Presidency playing an active role in safeguarding the principles and purposes of the UN Charter. He also expressed confidence that Khalil-ur-Rehman’s presidency of the General Assembly, unlike that of his predecessor, whose tenure was marked by harmful bias and politicization in the activities of the Presidency, would be based on a professional, balanced and responsible approach. Referring to the main theme of the 81st session of the General Assembly, “Rebuilding Trust in the United Nations,” the Foreign Minister noted that restoring trust in the United Nations above all requires ending gross violations of the fundamental principles of the UN Charter, particularly the principle of respect for the national sovereignty of states and the prohibition of the use of force set out in Article 2 of the Charter; preventing the instrumental use of the Security Council; and ending impunity for the perpetrators and those behind grave international crimes, particularly aggression, genocide and war crimes committed by the Zionist regime. The Foreign Minister briefed the President of the General Assembly on developments related to peace and security in the West Asia region following the military aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime against Iran. He stressed that the US-Israeli military aggression, which began on March 1, 2026, while nuclear negotiations were underway, and has continued to date in various forms, including a maritime blockade and economic sanctions, has no rationale other than bullying and the use of force. He added that the prevailing insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is also a result of these aggressive and interventionist actions. Mr. Khalil-ur-Rehman, for his part, expressed pleasure at meeting with the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran and reaffirmed his commitment to engaging professionally with all UN member states in carrying out the responsibilities of the General Assembly.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, participated Friday in the 27th Informal Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), chaired by Pakistan. Araghchi thanked Pakistan and the ECO Secretariat for organizing the meeting and emphasized the importance of strengthening regional cooperation among member states. Referring to the current state of the international system, Araghchi said the meeting was being held at a time when the world is facing growing uncertainty and fragmentation, while international law and international humanitarian law are increasingly being affected by acts of aggression. Referring to the US-Zionist military aggression against Iran over the past two years, the Iranian foreign minister said the Islamic Republic of Iran, despite its firm commitment to diplomacy and negotiations, has fallen victim to the illegal, aggressive and terrorist actions of the United States and the Israeli regime. Pointing to the material and moral damage caused by the military aggression of the United States and Israel against Iran, as well as the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, a number of senior military commanders, more than 4,000 Iranians, and 168 schoolchildren in the city of Minab, he added that numerous infrastructures, including hospitals, civilian airports and historic buildings, were targeted and damaged during the imposed war by the aggressors. Araghchi also referred to the resistance of Iran’s powerful armed forces and people, stressing that none of the aggressors’ sinister objectives were achieved thanks to the resistance of the Iranian people and the strength of the Armed Forces, and that Iran emerged from this historic test proud and more dignified than ever. The foreign minister went on to emphasize the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to enhance regional cooperation, saying Iran is committed to strengthening regional cooperation and solidarity and believes that ECO can play a more active role in promoting economic and trade cooperation, regional connectivity and sustainable development among its member states. Elsewhere in his remarks, Araghchi referred to recent developments within ECO and highlighted the resumption of several important meetings of the organization that had been suspended for several years, including ministerial meetings on trade, internal affairs and the environment. The foreign minister also cited the adoption of a five-year roadmap for cooperation in the mining sector, a 10-year strategy for sustainable and resilient transport in the ECO region, and the launch of the process to amend the ECO Trade Agreement (ECOTA) as examples of the member states’ collective determination to strengthen regional cooperation. Referring to the process of finalizing the ECO Vision for the coming decade, he expressed hope that the document would be considered and approved at the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran, with the aim of ensuring its feasibility, measurability and effective implementation. The foreign minister also described the development of transport infrastructure and regional connectivity as other important areas of cooperation among member states, saying the expansion of ECO corridors and their growing links with major freight and logistics hubs, including those connected to China, would strengthen the region’s role in international trade and transit networks. Araghchi described the growing trend of regional tourism and the expansion of intra-regional trade as signs of the gradual strengthening of the foundations of economic integration in the ECO region, while emphasizing that areas such as energy, human resources, agriculture and industry, and the environment remain among the region’s key priorities.Thanking the member states for their commitment and the efforts of the ECO Secretariat under Ambassador Majid Khan, he stressed the need to continue this process and make use of the organization’s capacities to advance the common objectives of its member states. In another part of his remarks, the foreign minister referred to the Islamic Republic of Iran’s hosting of the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran on December 3-4, 2026, emphasizing the importance of holding the summit at the highest level. Araghchi stressed that the valuable participation of the leaders of ECO member states in the summit could send an appropriate message to the peoples of the region and the international community. The foreign minister concluded by expressing hope that, through strengthened regional and multilateral cooperation, peace, security and prosperity would be further realized around the world and that unilateral coercive measures and acts of aggression that fuel instability and insecurity would come to an end.

item.title: Iranian Brunei Foreign Ministers meet on sidelines of UN General Assembly
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Brunei Foreign Minister Prince Abdul Mateen met on Thursday afternoon on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. During the meeting, the two sides discussed bilateral relations and international developments, particularly issues concerning the Muslim world, including Palestine and the genocide of Palestinians. Araghchi stressed the need for the Organization of Islamic Cooperation to pay greater attention to the issue of Palestine. Referring to the intensification of the occupying regime’s crimes against Palestinians in Gaza, the West Bank, Al-Quds and other parts of the occupied Palestinian territories, as well as the regime’s continued aggression against Lebanon and other Muslim countries, he underscored the need for urgent action to counter the Zionist regime’s colonial domination. The two sides also held consultations on Iran-Brunei bilateral relations.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while fully rejecting the baseless claims of the Government of Colombia against the Islamic Republic of Iran, strongly condemns the accusations leveled against a part of Iran’s official armed forces. The Government of Colombia’s action in making baseless accusations against Iran and simultaneously announcing the severance of diplomatic relations—which have a history of more than half a century—is contrary to the principle of mutual respect and incompatible with the interests and benefits of the two nations. It is clear that none of the claims raised by the Government of Colombia to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this decision has been taken solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States. The Government of Colombia, which, according to undeniable documents and evidence, has been heavily under the influence of drug-producing and drug-trafficking cartels and is in practice considered part of the sinister network of narcoterrorism in the American continent and beyond, is in no position whatsoever to preach to others about terrorism and narcotics. Such hypocritical deflection cannot absolve the Colombian Government of its international responsibility for participating in the trafficking of large shipments of narcotics to various parts of the world, including to Iran. The seizure in Tehran in late September of a 55-kilogram shipment of pure Colombian cocaine, which had been trafficked directly to Iran by a network linked to influential Colombian individuals, is one of the most recent discovered cases of transnational organized crime attributable to the Government of Colombia. It was expected that the relevant authorities of the Colombian Government, instead of reacting hastily to this matter, would cooperate within the framework of their international legal obligations to identify the principal elements involved in the trafficking of this shipment and similar shipments to Iran and other countries in the region. The Islamic Republic of Iran, in order to safeguard its national interests, will take the necessary measures in response to this unjustified and hostile approach by the Government of Colombia.
